Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

abuse verb and noun

misuse: use wrongly

also misuse, abuse of power, take advantage of, abuse someone’s patience

classical

Cic. Cat. 1.1: abūtēre, Catilīna, patientiā nostrā (Lewis & Short)
Cic. Verr. 2.5.113: lībertāte

abūtor, abūtī, abūsus sum

verb, third conjugation, deponent, with the ablative

misuse, abuse

Its first sense is to use up or to make full use of (ōtiō, to spend one’s leisure, Cic. Rep. 1.9); the bad sense, to misuse, is as classical. The thing misused is in the ablative.

Other words

  • male ūtor (+ ablative) — use badly

    phrase: male with ūtor, ūtī, ūsus sum and the ablative · also used · classical

    The plain opposite of bene ūtī: of a gift, a chance, one’s time.

Examples

  • quō ūsque tandem abūtēre, Catilīna, patientiā nostrā?

    how long, Catiline, will you go on abusing our patience?Cic. Cat. 1.1

  • Hem, verbōrum proprietāte semper abūteris!

    There you go again, misusing words!Cord. Coll. 4.23

See also abuse, abuse, use.
